<thought>We need to determine the number of methyl (CH₃) groups in the unknown compound. The only way to get structural information is to obtain its ¹H NMR spectrum, which will show signals for methyl protons (typically singlets, doublets, etc., around 0.8–1.2 ppm). By analyzing the spectrum we can count distinct methyl environments, which equals the number of CH₃ groups.</thought>
